column1: # The guard table of the golden corpus: a frozen copy of the foreman product's own (its ops/tests/guard.tsv), run
# against the [deny] list of tests/test_golden.py (FARO_DENY) through `foreman guard --table` and the guard hook.
# deny: publishing and the machine's shared setup, never without Owner (rules.md §2)
# deny: foreman's built-in rule, for everyone (the hooks module's ops never go through Bash)
# orchestrator: foreman's built-in rule for `permissions apply` (never an agent; --opens also asks the owner)
# deny: the reserved files, for a Write or Edit call of anyone; the orchestrator writes only its board
# orchestrator: the git class (hooks and config of git of a protected repo, and the machine's), an agent's only
# deny: a Bash command that writes a reserved file by name, for anyone; the orchestrator writes only its board
# allow: the daily work of the product
# The values of data arguments (note, progress, backlog, integrate's texts, guard, git commit -m) are text

column2: foreman --project foreman note "t" "nunca git remote add sin Owner"
FOREMAN_WHO=fo28 foreman --project foreman progress "hecho; git push es de Owner"
foreman --project foreman backlog add E1 --id AB-99 --title "x" --detail "a; uv publish; b"
foreman integrate foreman fo28/x "AB-28 T1" --note "sin npm publish ni git push" --result "ok"
foreman guard "git remote add origin x"
bin/foreman --project foreman note "t" "git push -u origin main"

foreman note "t" "$(cat <<'EOF'
git remote add origin x
git push
EOF
)"
git commit -m "docs: never git push here"

column1: # What still runs inside or next to a text command is compared

column2: foreman --project foreman note t x; git push
foreman note t x & git push
foreman note t \"; git push; echo \"
foreman backlog add E1 --id X --title "npm publish" | sh
foreman note x <(git push -u origin main)
foreman note t 'git remote add origin x

column1: # What runs inside (sh -c, eval, xargs, find -exec, ssh, heredocs, here-strings and pipes into a shell)

column2: bash -c "foreman note t 'git remote add origin x'"

cat <<'EOF' > ops/reviews/x.md
git push
git remote add origin x
EOF
git commit -F - <<'EOF'\ndocs: git push stays with Owner\nEOF

column1: # A heredoc to an interpreter that is not a shell is compared raw (an anchored pattern does not see it)
# A group or compound piped into a reader, or a variable in the program's place: the line is read as fed to a shell

column2: if true; then foreman note t "git push"; fi | sh
for x in 1; do echo "git push"; done | sh
echo "git push" | if true; then sh; fi
for c in "git push"; do $c; done
{ foreman note t "git push"; } | grep x
for f in a b; do echo "$f"; done | sort

column1: # echo/printf, the pattern of grep, rg and git grep, gh pr|issue --title/--body and git tag -m are text, and a printer may write to a literal path; what runs (a pipe or a substitution into a shell, a file written and run in the line, a device) is still compared

column2: printf 'git push\n' | tee x.sh; bash x.sh
echo "git push" | cat > x.sh && sh x.sh
printf 'nunca git push sin Owner\n' > ops/notes/x.md
printf '%s\n' "git remote add origin x" >> ops/reviews/x.md
echo "git push es de Owner" > ops/reviews/x.md
git tag -a v1.0.0 -m "sin git push todavía"
gh pr create --title "x" --body "after merge: npm publish"
gh issue comment 3 --body "git push stays with Owner"

column1: # python reading its program from a quoted heredoc is compared with its prose blanked when an allow-list
# gate says it cannot start a process (imports, names); one-word literals, and anything else, as before

column2:

p.write_text(p.read_text().replace("x", "nunca git push"))
EOF

EOF

EOF
